issue.close_reason:
Implemented the nonoverlapping daemon loop (plan Section 7.9) in crates/archivist-client-core/src/daemon.rs, wired into lib.rs and recorded in docs/notes/crate-ownership.md (commit 4950d58, pushed).

What the module is: run() starts the first cycle immediately and each later cycle one uniformly jittered delay after the previous cycle RETURNED - sequential by construction, so self-overlap is impossible without a lock; delays are drawn pure over [interval, interval + jitter_span) via tick_delay's 64-bit map (15 min, up to 10 percent from plan_defaults or ResolvedConfig's schedule keys); every wait is measured against a monotonic Instant deadline re-sliced at SLEEP_SLICE (100 ms), so a wall-clock step cannot lengthen, shorten, reorder, skip, or repeat a cycle; cancellation is honored between cycles (a cycle in flight finishes; a cancel stops the loop the moment it returns, before another delay is drawn; a cancel during sleep interrupts within one slice); the loop holds two words of bookkeeping (LoopReport) and persists nothing, so progress is whatever the cycle bodies make durable - a restart resumes it; a dead jitter source stops the loop rather than degrading into a synchronized fixed-period stampede.

Tests (all deterministic on a virtual clock, 22 in the module): jitter arithmetic (range, monotonicity, zero-jitter exactness, refusal of unrunnable intervals/jitter, config-loader refusal of a zero period and a 101-percent jitter by field name); immediate first cycle with jittered gaps; non-overlap proven by a reentrancy detector across 1000 cycles and a uniform 100k-cycle long run with flat bookkeeping; cancellation before start, during a cycle (finish + no further delay drawn), during sleep (prompt stop); restart continuing a shared durable cursor strictly incrementally; the clock-change acceptance - a wall clock lurching -1h/+2h after every cycle ends 3 h ahead of the monotonic timeline and moves nothing; the month-scale marathon (2619 cycles at the full-span tick) starting every cycle inside the month, each advancing exactly one bounded step, unable to fit another tick. The production ThreadSleeper is proven on bounded real waits (waits at least the delay, returns promptly on cancel, instantly when already cancelled).

Adopted the prior attempt's uncommitted WIP and repaired it: six of its tests failed and one hung when first run (it died on an API error before ever running them) - the loop now rechecks Cancel after a cycle returns, the half-open tick expectation is exact, the config tests assert the loader's refusal, and the endless scenario gained a wait budget; also fixed 17 pedantic clippy errors and one denied broken intra-doc link.

Verification ran inside a clean git-archive extraction of committed HEAD (4950d58) with a fresh target dir; all green, then pushed with origin/main..HEAD empty.
```verified:
scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast exit=0
cargo test -p archivist-client-core --lib daemon:: exit=0
cargo test -p archivist-client-core --lib exit=0
```
issue.description: Run the collection engine every 15 minutes with up to 10 percent jitter using monotonic timing and no self-overlap. Acceptance: restart, long-run, clock-change, cancellation, and month-scale marathon tests preserve incremental progress and bounded resource use.
issue.notes: Adopted the prior attempt's uncommitted daemon.rs + daemon/tests.rs WIP (attempt 01a0cd05 died on API error 499 before its tests ever ran) and landed it against HEAD: module wired into lib.rs with the Status-doc paragraph, crate-ownership.md row extended. Repairs the WIP needed: run() now rechecks Cancel immediately after a cycle returns (no entropy draw or wait request for a loop that will not run another cycle); tick_delay documented as a half-open span whose all-ones draw lands 1 ns under interval+span; from_resolved doc corrected (the config loader range-checks both schedule keys at load; the tests now assert the loader's Usage refusal by field name); VirtualSleeper gained a wait budget so the first-cycle scenario terminates; the missing clock-change acceptance test added (a wall clock lurching -1h/+2h per cycle leaves the schedule exactly the pure arithmetic and progress strictly incremental). Fixed 17 pedantic clippy errors (manual-let-else, useless u128 conversions, missing_panics_doc, duration_suboptimal_units, unchecked_time_subtraction, cast_possible_truncation) and one denied broken intra-doc link. Scope: library module only, like its sibling phase-5 surfaces; CLI composition attaches at the composition root, out of this bead's scope.

issue.description:
Split child 1/4 of aa-58802c04 (Implement the OpenCode source reader). In crates/archivist-adapter-opencode, add the store-connection module that opens the configured OpenCode SQLite database strictly read-only (read-only open mode; never creates or writes) with a five-second busy timeout, using the workspace rusqlite (bundled) already used by archivist-client-core. Keep the crate's internal dependency boundary: archivist-adapter-sdk only, no other internal crates (tools/check-crate-graph.py and the dependency-boundary tests must stay green). Map open-time outcomes onto the SDK's closed ScanClassification vocabulary (crates/archivist-adapter-sdk/src/status.rs): missing database file -> no-database, without creating a file; unreadable path -> permission-denied; a competing lock held past the busy window -> read-error.

Acceptance:
1. Opening a nonexistent database classifies no-database and leaves no new file on disk.
2. An unreadable (permission-denied) path classifies permission-denied.
3. A second connection holding a write lock yields read-error and the adapter never blocks the other writer; the production constant stays five seconds and tests may inject a shorter busy window to stay fast.
4. The opened connection cannot write: a write attempt fails.
5. This module reads no projected content and no database path or schema string reaches an error or status message (content-free, per docs/security/threats/adapter-capture.md content-freedom discipline).

Contract basis: plan Phase 6B and CAP-004; pre-claim evidence gate row "Database sources - OpenCode" (docs/security/threats/adapter-capture.md); AC-04 and AC-08.
issue.notes: Implemented in crates/archivist-adapter-opencode: store_connection module (src/store_connection.rs) + tests/store_connection.rs. SQLITE_BUSY past the busy window, forced by a sqlite_master schema probe that takes the read lock) is ReadError. BUSY_TIMEOUT=5s constant; open_with_busy_timeout lets tests inject 150ms. Unit-variant error type maps to ScanClassification; Display emits only the classification token, driver text dropped (content-free). Tests cover all five ACs incl. an honest skip when the process bypasses mode-000 (permissions row) and a hostile-path content-freedom negative. Manifest: rusqlite.workspace = true added to the adapter (crate-ownership rule 3 keeps external deps in-crate; dependency_boundary tests unaffected). Committed 9abc32a. Note: committed Cargo.lock carries one pre-existing ridealong line from concurrent work on this checkout (tokio in the archivist-cli lock entry, whose manifest edit is still uncommitted by the sibling worker); cargo prunes the stale entry on build. issue.description: Implement bounded, signed-record GET and HEAD operations for the ControlReadStore using only the dedicated control-prefix read identity. Acceptance: tenant scope, schema, authority signature, version, cache metadata, size, and error classification validate before a record reaches authorization code, with no raw or control-write authority.
issue.notes:
IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN (codinghome, 2026-09-19). Discovery is done; this is now
a typing job. Not implemented here -- handed back to the frontier.

## Why this bead is the critical path

It is the sole blocker on aa-35b2f2da (compose the serve entrypoint), which in
turn blocks aa-8be18fe5 and aa-9a986c02. IngestStorage::compose needs
W: RawWriteStore + C: ControlReadStore. W exists (raw_write.rs:465,
S3RawWriteStore). C has NO production implementation -- the only impls of
ControlReadStore in the workspace are #[cfg(test)] mocks at
archivist-storage/src/ingest.rs:210 and archivist-server/src/serve.rs:363.
Until this lands, nothing in the workspace can be composed into a server.

## The work is smaller than control_admin.rs suggests

control_admin.rs is 2349 lines because it enforces write classes: immutable
families rejecting incompatible objects, current-pointer families requiring a
strictly increasing signed epoch. The READER has none of that.

ControlRecord::new(envelope: Vec<u8>, observation: Observation) takes raw
bytes. There is NO parsing and NO signature verification in this layer. The
trait doc (control.rs, above line 291) is explicit: "Ok(Some(record)) hands
over unverified bytes; failing closed on a bad signature, a stale epoch, or an
expired cache entry is the consumer's contract (EC-09), not the store's", and
ControlRecord's own doc says "Verifying it is the consumer's job".

Note this bead's acceptance wording ("authority signature ... validate before
a record reaches authorization code") reads as if the store verifies. It does
not: that describes the end-to-end pipeline property, and the store's
contribution is tenant scope, size, cache metadata and error classification.
Do not add signature checks here -- it would contradict the trait contract and
duplicate the consumer.

## Design

New module crates/archivist-storage-s3/src/control_read.rs, registered in
lib.rs beside control_admin.

1. `pub trait ControlReadBackend` mirroring ControlAdminBackend's read half but
   returning metadata as well as bytes, because Observation needs it:

     fn get_control_object(&self, key: &ControlObjectKey)
       -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<ObservedObject>, StorageError>> + Send;

   with a small `ObservedObject { envelope: Vec<u8>, etag: Option<ObjectTag>,
   storage_version: Option<StorageVersionId> }`. ControlAdminBackend's
   get_control_object returns a bare Option<Vec<u8>> and is NOT reusable as-is.

2. `pub struct S3ControlReadStore<B>` holding the backend, the provisioned
   TenantId, a record-size ceiling, and a clock.

3. `impl<B: ControlReadBackend + Sync> ControlReadStore for S3ControlReadStore<B>`
   for all five methods, each the same shape:
     - tenant outside provisioning -> StorageError::ScopeViolation
     - derive the key by REUSING ControlObjectKey (control_admin.rs:133,
       already pub): linked_client / delegation / revocation / rotation /
       receipt_key map 1:1 onto the five trait methods. Reusing it is what
       guarantees reader and writer agree on keys; do not re-derive.
     - backend read; None -> Ok(None). An unlinked client and a missing
       delegation are ordinary states, not errors (trait doc).
     - oversize envelope -> StorageError::MalformedInput, bounded BEFORE the
       bytes are retained. Follow the KEY_MAX = 512 convention in
       control_admin.rs for naming the constant.
     - Ok(Some(ControlRecord::new(envelope, Observation::new(etag,
       storage_version, observed_at))))

4. Clock: Observation::observed_at is documented as "this store's own clock
   reading ... so cache bounds such as the 60-second trust-record TTL are
   computable without trusting any backend clock". control_admin has no clock
   (it parses Timestamp out of signed envelopes at line 441), so the reader
   introduces one. Inject it rather than calling the system clock, so the
   60-second TTL boundary is deterministically testable.

5. The trait has no read(key), no write, no delete, no list -- keep it that
   way. An ingest replica must not be able to enumerate or publish control
   records through its storage configuration.

## Tests to write

Per method: absent -> Ok(None); present -> byte-exact envelope with etag and
storage_version carried into Observation; foreign tenant -> ScopeViolation;
oversize -> MalformedInput; backend failure -> Unavailable. Plus one test
asserting the derived key equals what ControlObjectKey produces for the same
inputs, so reader/writer divergence fails loudly.

issue.notes:
Implemented the usage-summary derivation (plan Phase 10 producer core).

Commit d49543f (pushed to origin/main), 4 files:
- crates/archivist-protocol/src/usage_summary.rs (new): UsageSummary::derive — pure layer-0 function from the adapter projection's normalized per-message reading (MessageUsage: Measured(SourceUsageCounts) | Absent | Malformed | Unsupported, plus source-named model/tier) to the canonical record, its usage-summary-v1 digest (FrameBuilder framing over the record's own canonical bytes, digest member excluded from its own preimage), and the sharded derived object key. Unobserved routes never read as free: denominator precedence unsupported > malformed > measured > absent pinned in module docs — any unsupported region folds the whole denominator with both identity members omitted; any malformed region refuses the sum outright (never a partial sum over whatever parsed); a measured subset discloses partial coverage via assistant_message_count; zero included messages give unknown/absent. No count ever sits beside an unknown; explicit zeros stay observations inside measured. Identities fold on measured-branch disagreement or a non-representable reading; sums are checked arithmetic over the u63 wire domain.

issue.description:
GitOps repo: jedarden/declarative-config (Forgejo origin; NEVER kubectl apply).
Target cluster: iad-ci. ArgoCD Application: to be added to the iad-ci
ApplicationSet (k8s/iad-ci/iad-ci-applicationset.yml).
Manifest path: k8s/iad-ci/agent-archivist/

## Why iad-ci, and the tension to weigh before starting

ARMOR is ClusterIP-only in every cluster it runs in (iad-ci, rs-manager,
iad-kalshi) -- nothing exposes it on the tailnet. The ingest replicas hold the
ARMOR credentials and must reach it, so they must be CO-LOCATED with an ARMOR
deployment. That eliminates ardenone-cluster and every other cluster outright,
unless ARMOR is newly tailnet-exposed (a larger change, not assumed here).

Among the three ARMOR clusters, iad-ci is chosen for data gravity: the agent
transcript corpus this project archives already lives in its bucket under
`transcripts/`, and `k8s/iad-ci/armor/transcript-receiver-*` is an exact working
precedent for the tailnet-exposure half of this bead.

The tension, recorded so whoever picks this up can overturn it rather than
discover it: k8s/iad-ci/AGENTS.md says long-lived services "default to 50m/128Mi
and should normally live on another cluster", and iad-ci is a burst CI cluster
whose autoscaler and capacity are tuned for short workflow pods (a capacity
check on 2026-09-13 showed a largest-fitting pod of ~1.5-2.3 CPU and pods
already unschedulable). If that rules iad-ci out, rs-manager is the alternative
and the only change is the manifest path and bucket name -- not the design.

## Overlap to resolve, not ignore

`armor-transcript-receiver` already does a narrow version of this job: a
credential-free, write-only Envoy front door letting NEEDLE hosts archive
transcripts into ARMOR without holding a credential. agent-archivist's ingest
server is the designed superset of that role. Decide explicitly whether the two
coexist during the pilot or the receiver is retired, and record it; do not
silently stand up a second front door for the same corpus.

## Manifests

- namespace, Deployment (>= 2 replicas; the server is stateless by design,
  "No server-side recovery queue is required"), ClusterIP Service
- ExternalSecret delivering ONLY the control-reader and raw-writer identities
  from aa-adeab1be. The control-admin credential must never reach these pods.
- IngressRoute on Traefik's `vpn` entrypoint + Certificate + a DNSEndpoint in
  k8s/iad-ci/tailnet-external-dns/dnsendpoints.yaml, mirroring
  transcripts-iad-ci-ts.ardenone.com. Clients are tailnet hosts; the tailnet ACL
  is the "who may reach it" boundary, and the linked-client signature is the
  "who may write" boundary.
- Probes: /health/live for liveness ONLY (it is process-only by deliberate
  design so a storage outage cannot kill healthy pods), /health/ready for
  readiness. Readiness requires fresh trust evidence per tenant, so it stays
  false until aa-adeab1be has seeded control records -- expect and tolerate that
  during rollout.
- Metrics scrape for /metrics; resource requests on every container; image
  pinned to the semver in containers/agent-archivist/VERSION, never :latest.

## Blocked by

- aa-35b2f2da -- nothing runnable exists until the serve entrypoint is composed.
- aa-adeab1be -- the credentials and prefix layout this consumes.
- aa-580ffbb2 -- the published server image this pins.

## Acceptance

- ArgoCD reports the Application Synced and Healthy, and the live resources
  match the repo (no live kubectl mutation at any point).
- A tailnet host reaches the endpoint; /health/live is 200; /metrics returns the
  server families; POST /v1/ingest returns the stable 503 until the pipeline
  lands.
- Record the deployment commit on this bead before closing.
issue.title: Deploy the ingest replicas to iad-ci via declarative-config

issue.description:
Nothing in this workspace is runnable today. `crates/archivist-cli/src/main.rs`
is `fn main() {}` -- an honest Phase-0 skeleton, correctly carrying no stub
behaviour -- and it is the only [[bin]] in the workspace and the binary
`containers/agent-archivist/Dockerfile` builds. The release image starts, does
nothing, and exits 0.

The libraries are largely there. `archivist-server` is ~3,000 lines: the Axum
router mounts all four routes, `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/metrics`
are implemented, `serve.rs` has the bind/serve lifecycle, `ServerConfig` is 826
lines, and trust evaluation and Prometheus exposition are built.
`archivist-storage-s3` has the multipart writer, capability probe,
control-admin surface, audit reader and portable S3 config.

What is missing is composition, and there are two concrete gaps:

1. `crates/archivist-server/Cargo.toml` depends on `archivist-storage`
   (the interface) but NOT `archivist-storage-s3`. No concrete backend is
   reachable from the server.
2. `archivist-storage-s3` appears in `crates/archivist-cli/Cargo.toml` as a
   dependency edge that no code uses.

The CLI is the documented composition root -- "it selects the concrete storage
backend and the set of enabled source adapters and hands them to the library
crates" -- so the wiring belongs there, not in the server crate.

## Scope

Implement the `serve` command family (plan Section 6) far enough to run the
server that already exists:

- Construct the S3 storage backend from configuration and hand it to
  `ServerState`, keeping the control-reader and raw-writer identities separate
  as the plan's control-plane boundary requires -- two credentials, not one.
- Load `ServerConfig` through the documented precedence and fail closed on
  invalid trust or storage configuration.
- Run the existing bind/serve lifecycle with signal-driven cancellation.

Explicitly NOT in scope: the ingest pipeline. `/v1/ingest` stays fail-closed
with the stable retryable `server.unavailable` body until aa-840a9d28,
aa-d71d8140, aa-d95a3f12 and aa-fd7981b6 land. Replacing that handler is those
beads' work; this bead only makes the process exist.

## Relationship to aa-a70d0479

aa-a70d0479 ("Implement the server bootstrap surface") covers the server-side
configuration, Axum startup and route registration, most of which has shipped.
This bead is the CLI-side composition that turns those libraries into a
process. Neither subsumes the other; do not fold them together.

## Acceptance

- `archivist serve` binds, answers 200 on /health/live, serves real families on
  /metrics, and returns the stable 503 body on POST /v1/ingest.
- Invalid trust or storage configuration fails at startup with a content-safe
  error, never a partially-started process.
- `containers/agent-archivist/Dockerfile` builds a binary that runs the server
  as its entrypoint (it currently builds `--bin archivist` whose main is empty;
  confirm whether the image should invoke `archivist serve` or gain a second
  binary, and keep the reproducibility contract in
  docs/notes/release-container.md intact either way).

issue.description: Split child of aa-4e4a2929 (umbrella: Implement the S3 control administrator), continues from aa-ed0666fa. Prove the store-level write semantics of S3ControlAdminStore exercised through the ControlAdminStore trait seam against a permission-scoped in-memory backend. Acceptance criteria: (1) overwriting an immutable record with incompatible bytes fails; (2) replaying an identical immutable write is idempotent, not an error; (3) replacing a current-pointer record requires a strictly higher valid signed epoch — equal, lower, and invalid epochs fail closed before any backend write; (4) a corrupt stored pointer surfaces as an integrity conflict; (5) every store write lands inside the backend permission scope. Evidence lands as tests in crates/archivist-storage-s3 and must pass scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast on a clean git archive HEAD extraction.
issue.notes: Audited HEAD's evidence against the five acceptance criteria: criteria 1/2/4 and most of 3/5 were covered (immutable overwrite + idempotent replay per family from aa-6d7375d2, epoch gate from aa-7d3d052e, scope from aa-579d1270), but four edges had no case and the trait seam had no consumer anywhere. Closed: (a) a generic harness bound only to ControlAdminStore drives both write classes end to end in tests/control_admin_scope.rs - the first external consumer of the seam, with backend counters pinning one accepted put per immutable family, exactly the accepted pointer epochs, and every request granted inside the provisioned prefix with zero denials across accepted and refused writes alike; (b) immutable identity proven byte-exact including wrapper members (re-signed/re-timestamped variants conflict, per family); (c) the epoch, not the bytes, gates pointers - novel payload at the stored epoch is StaleEpoch, stale refusals assert no write issued, and invalid epochs are refused before any request at all (requests()==2 = the initial write's read+put); (d) a well-formed same-family stored record whose members re-derive to a different key is an IntegrityConflict (the pointer filter's key arm, previously unexercised), and corrupt-pointer refusals assert zero puts and unchanged stored bytes. Mutation-checked: relaxing the epoch gate to non-strict fails both the unit pointer test and the trait-seam harness. cargo fmt/clippy(-D warnings)/tests green for the crate; scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast PASS 24/24 on a clean git archive HEAD extraction of 6597daa (dedicated target dir, extraction removed after); manifest emitted and retained in ~/.needle/verification/aa-3c97a61d/. Immutable families (revocation, rotation, receipt-key) are written once at their derived key: an incompatible object at an occupied key is a conflict. issue.description:
Implement the production S3 request backend: a concrete type satisfying the RawWriteBackend seam (put, conditional put, multipart create/part/complete/abort) and the ControlReadBackend seam (bounded GET/HEAD with ObservedObject metadata) in crates/archivist-storage-s3 - and the ControlAdminBackend seam when the admin command family needs a live backend. The two stores (S3RawWriteStore, S3ControlReadStore, landed by aa-ebd9939c and aa-1b138356) are generic over these seams; the only existing impls are the #[cfg(test)] MapBackend/PolicyBackend mocks, and the storage compatibility suite (tests/storage_compatibility.rs) documents that "a real qualification run supplies the same profile description to a live S3 request seam". No production impl exists at HEAD 7753c70.

Constraints (verified against the tree):
- Request signing is cryptography: the SigV4-style signer belongs in archivist-auth per docs/notes/crate-ownership.md rule 5, not in the storage crate.
- Offline/vendored builds: any HTTP client, TLS, hash/HMAC, and response-parsing dependencies must be vendored (source replacement in .cargo/config.toml); Cargo.lock committed in the same change.
- Credentials resolve from CredentialReference (file:/env: grammar, crates/archivist-storage-s3/src/config.rs) at composition time; resolved values never appear in argv, logs, or transcripts.
- Bounded reads: control GET/HEAD responses are capped (envelope_max_bytes discipline); no unbounded buffering anywhere (repo-wide invariant).
- Prefix scope: the concrete binding over the raw-writer credential enforces the deployment's prefix scope (raw_write.rs documents this as deployment-side).
- No-delete invariant: the only destructive verb is multipart abort, pinned to the raw writer (tools/armor-identities.toml).
- Qualification: the MinIO reference profile in tools/storage-profiles.toml is the live qualification path for this backend.

Unblocks: aa-35b2f2da (serve entrypoint composition - hard-blocked because CommandHandler is a non-generic fn pointer, so the binary must name a concrete backend type). Also gives the admin command family (aa-aa24ad95, aa-8a83d5cd) a live backend for end-to-end qualification; those beads currently verify over mock seams and are not hard-blocked.

Scope note: this bead is the request transport only - capability probing, the synthetic compatibility suite, and ingest reads are the remaining slices named in crates/archivist-storage-s3/src/lib.rs and stay out of scope here.
issue.notes: Implemented S3RequestBackend in crates/archivist-storage-s3/src/request.rs for raw PUT, conditional PUT, multipart create/part/complete/abort, bounded control GET/HEAD with ObservedObject metadata, and ControlAdmin GET/PUT. Added composition-time file/env credential resolution with redacted SigV4 credentials; SigV4 signing lives in archivist-auth/src/sigv4.rs. Enforced tenant/prefix authority scope, bounded response bodies, timeout, status classification, and the raw-writer-only DELETE abort path. issue.description:
Every control record in this system is signed by a tenant authority, and
nothing in the repository creates one.

## Evidence

- tools/cli-commands.toml declares 9 commands (`admin approve`, `admin
  delegate`, `admin receipt-key`, `admin revoke`, `admin rotate`, `catalog
  rebuild`, `link request`, `verify-state`). Every one ASSUMES the authority
  already exists: `admin approve` is summarised as "validate the draft, sign
  it with the tenant authority, and write the linked-client record", and
  `admin receipt-key` as "generate and certify a tenant receipt-signing key
  under the pinned tenant authority chain".
- No registry command creates or certifies the authority itself.
- docs/notes/control-trust.md and docs/notes/cli.md contain no
  create/generate/mint/bootstrap procedure for it.
- No bead owns it. Searching the graph for tenant-authority / trust-root /
  bootstrap returns only record schemas (aa-c89db275, aa-8aa7f917), record
  signing (aa-b670ef2f), rotation (aa-cb5a534f), and the SERVER bootstrap
  surface (aa-a70d0479), which is the ingest process starting up -- an
  unrelated sense of the word.

The plan's control-plane boundary says "The initial administrator CLI writes
tenant-authority-signed client, key, scope, delegation, revocation, and
receipt-verification-key records to a dedicated S3 prefix." The store side is
built (aa-4e4a2929 closed). The key that signs them has no origin.

## Why this is a hard stop for adoption and not for us

This fleet can create an authority by hand once and never think about it
again. A third party cannot: with no authority they cannot link a client,
with no linked client the server authorizes no upload, and /health/ready
never reports ready. The first thing a new operator must do is the one thing
no command performs.

## Scope

Own the seam between the Phase 3 control-plane records and an operator who has
nothing yet:

1. Add the missing command(s) to tools/cli-commands.toml -- authority
   creation, and if the design wants them separable, certification/export of
   the public half that ingest replicas are configured with. Registry schema
   v1 is append-only, so adding a command is a compatible change; renaming an
   existing one is a v2 event.
2. Implement them. The `archivist` binary currently has NO argument parser at
   all (`fn main() {}`, no clap, no Subcommand), so this depends on the
   composition root -- see aa-35b2f2da.
3. Private authority material must never be echoed, logged, or written outside
   a mode-restricted path, consistent with aa-6f7c2010 and aa-d4cbc65a.
4. An executable end-to-end proof starting from an EMPTY bucket: create
   authority -> link a client -> accept one upload -> validate the receipt ->
   readiness reports ready. That proof is the acceptance test for "a stranger
   can actually start", and it is the artifact the adopter quickstart is
   written from.

## Acceptance

- A fresh operator, with no pre-existing records and no access to this fleet's
  state, can establish a trust root and reach a validated first receipt using
  only released commands.
- The proof runs in CI against the MinIO reference profile (aa-1b6a2063) so it
  keeps working for backends we do not host.
- No private authority material appears in any log, terminal, or committed
  file; the secret-hygiene tests cover the new paths.
issue.title: Own the zero-state bootstrap: a new adopter has no supported way to create a tenant authority

issue.notes: Extended the committed corpus replay over child 1's (aa-5135a79c) surfaces, test-file changes only. Coverage: (1) resolve_active_authority anchors the corpus chain at its newest half — tip key ID and public half proven against the last link's own members, established_at equal to that link's signed_at, retired_at none, the destination walk (resolve_authority to the tip) resolving the identical anchor, and the anchor's verify_signing_at agreeing with every corpus acceptance case naming the newest half; (2) a pinned root with no links served anchors itself (pinned, never established, retired by nothing, signing at an instant the corpus pins as root-accepted); (3) verify_control_record_resolved with the resolver verify_control_record itself installs reproduces every corpus record decision identically (same resolution on acceptance, same error class on rejection) and keeps the corpus's pinned verdict; (4) adversarial bundles fail closed through both the active walk and the seam path: a tampered mid-chain link (corpus last-link bytes with signed_at altered, served at the mid half's address) breaks both surfaces with Signature, and a looping succession (a link at the newest half's address re-establishing the pinned root) refuses both with ChainRule — the loop link is signed by regenerating the tip half from the seed the corpus's generation note documents (one byte 0x03 repeated 32 times), asserted equal to the corpus's own newest half, and both adversarial records still verify against the honest chain as positive controls. Key finding: the corpus cannot itself contain loop material (its honesty is the walk's termination argument), but its generation note publishing the synthetic seeds (0x01-0x04, 0x5c) is exactly what lets an adversarial bundle loop the real corpus chain rather than an invented one. Verified on a git-archive extraction of HEAD plus the test file (shared tree carries foreign WIP): 8/8 tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean, rustfmt clean. Committed 656f86d, pushed to origin.

issue.description:
README.md is a contributor and architecture document. Its sections are
Workspace, Documents, Governance, Design principles, Status, License. There is
no Install, no Quickstart, no "deploy this yourself", and no entry point for
someone who wants to run Agent Archivist rather than develop it.

No bead owned this. A graph search for quickstart / getting-started / readme /
onboarding / install / adopt returns 21 keyword matches, all false positives
("Implement installation identity generation", "Publish the stable support
policy", and similar).

## Why it matters for this project specifically

The plan's non-goals include "Requiring Kubernetes, ARMOR, B2, or one cloud
provider -- those are deployment profiles behind the public protocol and S3
contract". That is an explicit promise of third-party deployability, and
Phase 7 builds the artifacts to honour it (Helm aa-4c5d1c06, Compose
aa-c2e7acf5, systemd aa-f5bc4da6, storage profiles aa-96d56912, runbooks
aa-fa875ea2). None of that is reachable by a stranger without a document that
starts at zero.

## Scope

An adopter path that assumes no knowledge of this fleet, this plan, or these
docs/notes files:

- What the thing is and what it collects, in a paragraph.
- Prerequisites, honestly stated -- including the ones the definition-of-done
  gate needs that CONTRIBUTING under-declared (see aa-db9f9395).
- Install from a released artifact, not a git checkout: the signed OCI image
  (aa-e6e693b9) or Linux archive (aa-89b711f8).
- Stand up storage they control. MinIO is the reference profile
  (aa-1b6a2063); do not make ARMOR or B2 look required, because the plan says
  they are not.
- Bootstrap a trust root, link a client, and get one upload accepted and its
  receipt verified. That sequence comes from aa-8be18fe5, which is why this
  bead is blocked on it.
- Where to go next: configuration reference, runbooks, support policy
  (aa-f3815548).

## Do not write it early

A quickstart written against today's code would be fiction: the `archivist`
binary is `fn main() {}` with no argument parser, /v1/ingest is deliberately
fail-closed with 503, and ronaldraygun/agent-archivist has never been
published at any tag. Blocked on aa-8be18fe5 and aa-35b2f2da for that reason.

## Acceptance

- Someone who has never seen this repository can go from nothing to a running
  instance and a verified first upload using only README.md and what it links.
- Every command in it is copy-pasteable and exercised in CI, so the quickstart
  cannot silently rot -- the same reason the conformance corpus exists.
- It names no host, bucket, cluster, or credential belonging to this fleet.
issue.title: Write the adopter-facing README and quickstart: nothing today tells a stranger how to deploy this

issue.description:
CFG-001 claims the registry (tools/config-keys.toml, enforced by tools/check-config.py) is the complete configuration surface — "a setting that is not a registered key is not configuration and MUST NOT be read from a file, the environment, or a flag" — but registry v1 cannot express an optional *_ref secret key, so optional credential roles currently live as Option fields in the crate types, off-registry. - Phase 0: foundation, policy, fixtures, verification, and delivery baseline

- Phase 7: signed packaging, Compose, Helm, systemd, backup, profiles, runbooks, and observability
- Phase 8: comparator, shadow pilot, recovery, largest-history expansion, soak, restore, rollback, cutover, and legacy retention
- Phase 9: exact artifacts, expectation ledger, proxy, observer, Rust integration, correlation, flush, reconstruction, and coverage
- Phase 10: deterministic catalog, inventories, reports, retention, export, deletion, redaction, assessment, policy, and use authorization
- Phase 11: independent review, scans, fuzzing, production soak, compatibility, support, qualification, and stable publication
- Releases: execute 0.1 through 0.8 previews/candidates and the qualified, signed 1.0 stable release

Completion requires every live blocker to close with its own acceptance evidence, every plan definition-of-done item to pass on the evaluated commit, and the immutable 1.0 release to be published. There are no deliberate unresolved decision beads or deferred graph defects.

issue.description:
Storage backend decision: ARMOR (S3-compatible encrypting proxy) over Backblaze
B2, with prefix isolation. ARMOR encrypts before anything leaves it, so B2 holds
ciphertext only, and downloads route through Cloudflare at zero egress.

## Why ARMOR rather than Garage

The plan's control-plane boundary requires four identities with disjoint
action-by-prefix policy. `GarageKey` grants read/write/owner per BUCKET with no
prefix scoping, and Garage's write permission includes DELETE -- it can express
neither half of the requirement. ARMOR ACLs are `<bucket>:<prefix>:<verbs>`
with verbs drawn from {get, put, delete, list} (ADR-012, shipped: see
`internal/acl/acl.go` CheckACL(cred, bucket, key, verb) and the production
credential `iad-ci:transcripts/*:put`), which expresses both.

## Prefix layout

Under the ARMOR bucket, one tenant-scoped tree:

    agent-archivist/raw/       blobs, occurrence manifests, upload attestations
    agent-archivist/control/   tenant-authority-signed trust records
    agent-archivist/catalog/   reserved, Phase 10
    agent-archivist/derived/   reserved, Phase 10

## Identities

| Role | ACL | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| control reader | `<bucket>:agent-archivist/control/*:get+list` | ingest replicas |
| raw writer | `<bucket>:agent-archivist/raw/*:put+list` (+abort, see below) | ingest replicas |
| control admin | `<bucket>:agent-archivist/control/*:put+list` | offline admin CLI only |
| backup/restore | read across the tenant tree | offline |

Ingest replicas receive the first two ONLY. The plan is explicit: "Ingest
replicas never receive this credential" about the control-admin identity.

## Known constraint -- raw writer and abort

ARMOR maps AbortMultipartUpload to the Delete verb, alongside DeleteObject and
DeleteObjects. The plan requires the raw writer to abort but NOT to delete, and
the server aborts whenever size, expansion-ratio, media or digest validation
fails, so abort is on the normal path. Granting `delete` to satisfy abort would
let the ingest replica erase committed blobs, occurrences and attestations.

Tracked in the ARMOR workspace as armor-7bee0797 (add a distinct abort verb,
backward compatible). Do not provision the raw writer with `delete` as a
workaround without recording it as an accepted deviation in
docs/notes/ -- it removes the immutability guarantee the archive rests on.

## Provisioning mechanism

ARMOR loads named credentials from a single YAML document via `ARMOR_AUTH_FILE`
and hot-reloads it, so adding credentials needs no ARMOR Deployment change. The
document lives in OpenBao (for the iad-ci deployment:
`rs-manager/iad-ci/armor/credentials`) and reaches the pod through the
`armor-credentials-externalsecret` ExternalSecret. Follow
ARMOR docs/named-credential-provisioning-spec.md.

Credential values never become agent-visible text: generate them in place and
pipe into OpenBao under the write-only provisioning identity
(`bao-as <inst>-provision ... key=-`), never as a command-line literal. The
deliverable of this bead is the set of OpenBao PATHS plus the ACL strings, not
any value.

## Acceptance

- Each identity can perform exactly its ACL's operations under its prefix and
  is refused everything else, proven by a positive and a negative call per role.
- The control reader is refused any write; the raw writer is refused any read
  of a committed object and any cross-prefix access.
- Verification is by property -- `bao kv metadata get` for existence and a live
  ARMOR call for authorization -- never by printing a value.

standard-library only. That is not true, and a clean environment proves it.

## Evidence

First run of the new iad-ci gate (workflow agent-archivist-ci-manual-kbssg,
commit e3c6d045, debian:bookworm + python3, nothing else) came back with 25
of 28 checks green and these three red:

  FAIL control trust schemas   No module named 'jsonschema'
  FAIL conformance corpus      No module named 'cryptography'
  FAIL compat corpus           jsonschema is not installed

The real third-party imports across tools/ are jsonschema, cryptography and
referencing. They do not appear in a top-of-file import scan because they are
function-local: tools/conformancegen.py imports cryptography inside
SigningKey.__init__, and the schema gates import jsonschema inside their
check functions.

This went unnoticed because aa-0416e563 validated prerequisites against the
worker boxes -- its closing note reads "Lab worker box confirmed to have
gitleaks + cargo-audit + python3, so fast-lane membership is fleet-safe" --
rather than against a machine that had never run the gate. codinghome and the
lab both happen to have all three packages installed globally, so every local
and NEEDLE run passes while a fresh clone by a human developer does not.

## Fix

Two parts, both needed:

1. Declare the real prerequisites in CONTRIBUTING.md (and README where it
   lists them), with the versions the gate is known-good against --
   jsonschema 4.26.0 and cryptography 46.0.5 are what codinghome runs and what
   iad-ci now pins. Note that Debian bookworm's python3-jsonschema (4.10)
   predates the referencing-based resolver these tools use and cannot be used.

2. Make a missing python module fail the way a missing binary already does.
   require_tool() in scripts/definition-of-done.sh treats an absent scanner as
   a loud FAIL rather than a skip, on the stated principle that "the gate must
   not pass because a scanner was absent" -- but that check only covers
   executables. A missing module currently surfaces as a raw traceback, or, in
   the compat-corpus case, as "instance validation skipped", which is exactly
   the silent-hollow-check shape require_tool exists to prevent. Add the
   equivalent module-level preflight so the gate names the missing package.

## Acceptance

A container with only a Rust toolchain, python3, gitleaks and cargo-audit
runs scripts/definition-of-done.sh --all and either passes every check, or
names each missing prerequisite package explicitly. No check reports "skipped".

## Reference

The iad-ci template already works around this by pinning both packages in a
venv (declarative-config commit d3a9eab1); that is CI's own environment and
does not substitute for declaring the prerequisite in this repo.

Landed the bounded transport-decode stage (aa-2380d921), adopting and finishing this bead's prior attempt WIP (died api_error 499 mid-pass; trace .beads/traces/aa-2380d921). Commit b0f7ef6 stages exactly two files: crates/archivist-server/src/transport.rs (new) and crates/archivist-server/src/lib.rs (module wiring + crate-doc paragraph).

What the stage is: TransportDecoder<R: io::Read> yields bounded canonical chunks (16 MiB target) from the declared TransportEncoding - identity pass-through, or exactly one Zstandard frame through child-1's ZstdV1Decoder, whose DECODER_WINDOW_LOG_MAX cap rejects a hostile window before any allocation, verifies the embedded checksum during read-back, and fails bytes past the one frame. Both hard limits fire mid-stream against produced-byte totals, checked after every 256-byte feed slice: past record_max_bytes (256 MiB default) -> RecordTooLarge (request.record_too_large); cumulative canonical > ratio x transport (100:1 default) -> ExpansionRatioExceeded (request.expansion_ratio_exceeded); both carry PayloadLimit values for the routes' existing 413 rendering - exact-at-cap lawful, first byte past refuses. Malformed frames (truncated, hostile-window, lying-content-size, trailing bytes, empty body) fail closed with the codec's static detail under request.framing_invalid; SourceRead carries io::ErrorKind; CodecSetup -> server.internal. Buffers are the chunk Vec, the stack feed slice, and the window-capped decoder - nothing scales with body size, and a violating frame adds at most one Zstandard block ceiling (~8 MiB) between guard checks, so the ratio is computed over streamed bytes and a small compressed body cannot balloon memory before the guard fires (newly asserted: canonical at fire == payload, transport consumed <= one feed slice). A failed stage is closed - it re-yields its first error and never reads the source again. Abort-before-commit is pinned against a store double through MultipartWriter: over-cap attempts end in writer.abort() with commits==0, aborts==1, live_count==0; at-cap attempts stream and commit exactly once.

What the module is: run() starts the first cycle immediately and each later cycle one uniformly jittered delay after the previous cycle RETURNED - sequential by construction, so self-overlap is impossible without a lock; delays are drawn pure over [interval, interval + jitter_span) via tick_delay's 64-bit map (15 min, up to 10 percent from plan_defaults or ResolvedConfig's schedule keys); every wait is measured against a monotonic Instant deadline re-sliced at SLEEP_SLICE (100 ms), so a wall-clock step cannot lengthen, shorten, reorder, skip, or repeat a cycle; cancellation is honored between cycles (a cycle in flight finishes; a cancel stops the loop the moment it returns, before another delay is drawn; a cancel during sleep interrupts within one slice); the loop holds two words of bookkeeping (LoopReport) and persists nothing, so progress is whatever the cycle bodies make durable - a restart resumes it; a dead jitter source stops the loop rather than degrading into a synchronized fixed-period stampede.
